identificationModule.briefTitle: Study of Methylnaltrexone (MNTX) for the Relief of Constipation
identificationModule.officialTitle: A Double-Blind, Phase 3, Two-Week, Placebo Controlled Study of Methylnaltrexone(MNTX) for the Relief of Constipation Due to Opioid Therapy in Advance Medical Illness.

collaborators.name: Wyeth is now a wholly owned subsidiary of Pfizer

descriptionModule.briefSummary: To determine the efficacy of subcutaneous MNTX to relieve opioid-induced constipation in patients with advanced medical illness.
descriptionModule.detailedDescription: This is a multi-center, double-blind, randomized parallel group study conducted in patients with advanced medical illness and opioid-induced constipation. Eligible patients are randomly assigned to receive SC doses of either MNTX, dose 1 or placebo every other day for 2 weeks. At Day 8, eligible patients, if allowed, could be escalated to a a higher dose of MNTX.

primaryOutcomes.measure: Laxation within four hours of a single dose of SC MNTX and efficacy of SC MNTX every other day over a 1 week period.
primaryOutcomes.description:
To determine the efficacy of a single dose of SC MNTX compared with placebo in inducing laxation within 4 hours.

To determine the efficacy of SC MNTX every other day over a 1-week treatment period in relieving OIC in patients with AMI.

eligibilityModule.eligibilityCriteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* 18 years of age and older
* Negative pregnancy test (serum or urine) at screening for all women of childbearing potential
* Advanced Medical Illness (i.e., terminal illness, such as incurable cancer or end of stage AIDS) with life expectancy of ≥ 1 month
* patient must sign ICF

Exclusion Criteria:

* Women who are pregnant and/or nursing
* Previous treatment with MNTX
* Participation in any other studies involving investigational products within 30 days prior to screening
